content:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU utilization > 95% in pool 'prod-gpu-a' and autoscaler hit hard cap. Queue growth detected. potential service degradation. paging oncall.

tess (oncall-sre): i’m on it. seeing sustained enqueue rates, backlog up 12k requests. linking logs

tess (oncall-sre): log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:15:03Z [gpu-pool-prod-gpu-a] enqueue=12437 in_flight=2048 gpu_util=96% autoscaler_max_reached=true
2026-03-15T02:15:05Z [kvcache] mem_delta=+78GB active_contexts=5600
```

maria (ml-eng): this started right after the v25 rollout ~02:05. we pushed a tokenization/context change that increases kv cache retention for long-chat sessions. suspecting context retention growth.

raj (infra): autoscaler shows max_instances = 80 applied to that pool, we've exhausted quota for that region. cloud provider is not granting more instances due to soft limit.

olivia (prod-sre): customers are seeing 503s and big latency spikes (p95 > 8s). support dashboard shows elevated error rates from playbooks. lee, can you flag critical accounts?

lee (customer-ops): flagged 3 enterprise tenants on the watchlist. they're reporting increased latency and timeouts. raising priority with account teams.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01. severity=SEV2. linked runbook: gpu-exhaustion

maria (ml-eng): quick telemetry: model v25 average ctx_length jumped from 2.2K to 7.8K for active sessions; kv-layer growth correlates with v25 prefixes. this is likely the root.

tess (oncall-sre): mitigation options: 1) roll back v25 canary 2) throttle traffic to v25 3) enable emergency pool with different instance type and smaller KV retention. we should do the fastest-low-risk first.

raj (infra): we can spin an emergency pool in another region but coldstart will be ~4-6m. also need to update routing rules.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for model v25 was marked "promote" at 2026-03-15T02:04:52 by maria. shard split: 25% traffic.

olivia (prod-sre): do we have an immediate toggle to shift canary back to v24? if yes, do that now.

maria (ml-eng): i can toggle the routing config. pausing promotion and reverting traffic to v24 now. executing:
```
# rollback canary
redwoodctl routing set --model v25 --weight 0 --env prod
redwoodctl routing set --model v24 --weight 100 --env prod
```

maria (ml-eng): done. config applied. waiting for traffic shift.

tess (oncall-sre): observed ingress to v25 dropping to 0. enqueue still high, but in_flight decreasing slowly — kv warm entries persist.

raj (infra): creating emergency nodes (spot fallback) in region-us-west-2 to absorb backlog. command submitted to cloud provider. ETA 5m.

olivia (prod-sre): also enabling soft throttle for best-effort traffic to reduce queue growth: applying rate-limit window on /generate for non-enterprise routes.

olivia (prod-sre): command:
```
redwoodctl rate-limit --route "/generate" --max-rps 12000 --scope non_enterprise
```

tess (oncall-sre): key metric: kv_cache_mem_total peaked at +92GB. eviction running but cold KV evictions are slow; we might need to force-sweep older contexts. maria, can model config help evict earlier?

maria (ml-eng): we can flip a shorter context retention flag on v25, but v25 not receiving production traffic now. forcing eviction on workers possible via admin endpoint but risky. prefer organic decay after traffic shift + emergency capacity.

olivia (prod-sre): support update to customers: "We are experiencing degraded response times and increased errors for generation endpoints due to an internal model rollout. Mitigations in progress — traffic has been shifted away from the new model; we're adding capacity and applying rate-limits. We'll update every 15 minutes." (sending now)

support-bot: sent customer notification to affected accounts. incident channel updated.

raj (infra): emergency nodes reporting online. adding 12 nodes. smoothing into pool.

tess (oncall-sre): good, in_flight dropped from 2048 -> 1200 in the last 3m. queue length trending down. p95 latency improving from 8s -> 3.2s for non-enterprise.

lee (customer-ops): enterprise tenants still see intermittent timeouts, but less severe. they're on standby for a follow-up call.

maria (ml-eng): we should schedule a rollback of the v25 change that increased prefix retention or tune kv retention defaults. immediate follow-up: revert tokenizer/context change on v25 and re-run canary in staging with synthetic long-context load.

olivia (prod-sre): agree. action items: (1) revert v25 change in repo (maria), (2) request provider quota increase (raj), (3) postmortem and improved canary load tests (tess + eng-ml), (4) add autoscaler headroom guard to avoid hard cap being single point of failure (olivia).

maria (ml-eng): i've opened PR to revert the retention change: PR#5823. holding off on re-promote until we have new load tests.

raj (infra): quota request submitted; cloud support case #CS-99832. ETA 24-48h for approval but we will follow up with enterprise contacts.

tess (oncall-sre): current status: traffic reverted, emergency nodes helping, queue dropping steadily. marking this incident as mitigated but keeping channel open for verification.

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-0315-01 status: mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded to SEV3. timeline will be posted to the incident tracker.

olivia (prod-sre): final notes for now: delta in customer error rate reduced to baseline ~40m after rollback. we will draft communications for impacted customers tomorrow; retention tuning and improved canary are blockers before re-release.

lee (customer-ops): copied. prepping hour-follow-up to enterprise teams.

tess (oncall-sre): thanks all. will capture logs and attach to INC ticket. retrospective scheduled: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.

maria (ml-eng): sorry for the churn — will add stress tests for long-chat context in canary harness. thanks for the fast responses :heart:

support-bot: channel archived when incident closed.
